extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent Office examiners, OPLA staff, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) seeking guidance on search documentation and public-use petition handling
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and documentary standards for recording search activity in the application file wrapper (SEARCHED / SEARCH NOTES) and the formal/timeliness/substantive requirements and handling steps for petitions under 37 CFR 1.292 (public use/on-sale petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Search endorsement (first action)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits the examiner shall make an initial endorsement in black ink, in the space provided on the right outside panel of the file wrapper, of the classes and subclasses of domestic and foreign patents, abstract collections, and publications in which the search for prior art was made. The examiner must also indicate the date(s) on which the search was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other information collections and sources in which the search for prior art was made must also be identified. Great care should be taken so as to clearly indicate the places searched and the date(s) on which the search was conducted. In subsequent actions where the search is updated, the examiner must endorse and initial that the search has been updated and/or identify the additional field of search, including databases and search queries/classifications employed in the original search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate SEARCHED vs SEARCH NOTES entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches are separated into two categories and listed, as appropriate, in either the 'SEARCHED' box or 'SEARCH NOTES' box on the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search entries made here, except those for search updates, will be printed under 'Field of Search' on the patent front page. Entries intended to complete the application file record but not printed should go in SEARCH NOTES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete subclass search (record in 'SEARCHED')
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete search of a subclass, including all United States and foreign patent documents, whether filed by U.S. or IPC classification, and other publications placed therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complete classification (class and subclass) should be recorded. Examples: '424/270, 272, 273', 'A61K 31/56 - A61K 31/585'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited subclass search (record in 'SEARCHED' or 'SEARCH NOTES' depending)
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited search of a subclass restricted to an identifiable portion of the patent documents placed therein. If only the publications in a subclass are searched, the entry is to be made under 'SEARCH NOTES' rather than under 'SEARCHED'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the class and subclass followed by the information defining the portion searched in parentheses. Examples: '414/1 (U.S. only)', '238/6 (1954 to date)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search update entries (mark as '(updated)')
rubrics_metrics.description: An update of a search previously made should be recorded indicating which previously recorded searches have been updated, followed by the expression '(updated)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search update entries are recorded in the 'SEARCHED' box but will not be printed. When updating from a parent application, record ' (updated from parent S.N. ...)' or ' (updated from parent Pat. N. ...)' and recopy the relevant parent search onto the continuing application's file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' - cursory searches
rubrics_metrics.description: A cursory search, or scanning, of a U.S. subclass or IPC subclass/group/subgroup (usually made to determine if the documents classified there are relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the classification followed by '(cursory)'. Examples: '250/13 (cursory)', 'A61K 9/44 (cursory)'. Entries in SEARCH NOTES are of equal importance to those in SEARCHED but are not printed on the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' - consultations with other examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: A consultation with other examiners to determine if relevant search fields exist in their areas of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subclass is not searched, record the class and subclass discussed followed by '(consulted)'. May include the name of the examiner consulted and the art unit. Examples: '24/ fasteners (consulted J. Doe A.U. 3501)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' - literature/publication searches
rubrics_metrics.description: A search of a publication not located within the classified patent file (library, textbook, Chemical Abstracts, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record specifics depending on type: (1) Abstracting publications: name, list terms consulted, period covered (e.g., 'Chem. Abs, Palladium hydride Jan.-June 1975'); (2) Periodicals: title and period/volumes covered (e.g., 'Popular Mechanics, June-Dec. 1974'); (3) Books: title, author, edition/date; (4) Other literature (catalogs, manufacturer's literature): provide unique identification. Cursory browsing through many materials may be indicated collectively, but detailed reviews should be specifically recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' - publications only searches
rubrics_metrics.description: A search of only the publications in a subclass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record class and subclass followed by '(publications only)'. Examples: '43/56 (publications only)'. If only publications in a subclass were searched, place the entry in SEARCH NOTES rather than SEARCHED.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' - review of references cited in parent/original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of art cited in a parent application or an original patent, required for continuations, CIPs, divisionals, reissue, and reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the application number or patent number followed by 'refs. checked' or 'refs. ck'ed.' Note and record exceptions if some references were not checked because unavailable or clearly not relevant. Examples: 'S. N. 495,123 refs. checked', 'Pat. 3,900,000 refs. checked'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-accessed database searches: minimum documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions involving a search of a computer accessed text, chemical structure, or sequence database, the examiner shall endorse in the SEARCH NOTES box the minimum information: (1) the search logic or chemical structure or sequence used as a query; (2) the name of the file or files searched and the database service; (3) date of the search; and (4) the examiner's initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three acceptable methods to provide the minimum documentation: (1) supplying (and annotating as necessary) the computer search printout; (2) recording the required information on Search Request Form PTO-1590; or (3) recording the required information in the SEARCH NOTES box. For methods (1) and (2), record the database service name and the expression '(see form)' or '(see printout)' in SEARCH NOTES with the date and the examiner's initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printout handling and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: When supplying computer search printouts, the statement(s) of the history that produced results reviewed should be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several search statements appear in the history, circle in BLACK INK the statement(s) whose results were reviewed. Hole punch and place the form or printout page(s) with required data elements in the application file on the right-hand flap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database history commands and supplementation of missing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some database services do not display all required documentation elements with their history command (e.g., name of database service, date of search, file name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document missing elements by writing them on the printout or supplying further portions of the search transcript (e.g., log off command). The file name (not just file number) is required. If a service does not provide the date with the history command (e.g., WEST), the date must be written on the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide/peptide sequence search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide and peptide sequence searches must be fully documented by a printout of the search query sequence and the beginning of the search result file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each query sequence should be clearly related to the appropriate search result, if necessary by appropriate annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other publicly accessible databases (CD-ROM etc.) documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For other types of publicly accessible computer accessed databases (CD-ROMs, specialized databases), record data necessary to uniquely identify material searched and sufficient information about the search query to allow updating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also document the database location and its form (e.g., 'Entrez: Sequences, NCBI, Version 7.19.91b (CD-ROM, TC 1600) Searched HIV and vaccine; neighbored Galloway article dated 6/5/91 on April 1, 1990').

rubrics_metrics.name: Information not recorded on file wrapper (IDS consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain indications of consideration or nonconsideration of prior art citations submitted in Information Disclosure Statements are not recorded on the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 609 for guidance on recording consideration/nonconsideration of IDS citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.292
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public other than the applicant, including private persons, corporate entities, and government agencies, may file a petition for institution of public use proceedings. An attorney or representative may file on behalf of an unnamed principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions filed by parties to an interference as to an application involved in the interference are generally not allowed (see later inter partes rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal entry requirements for a public use petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition and accompanying papers, or a notice that such a petition has been filed, shall be entered in the application file if: (1) the petition is accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(j); (2) the petition is served on the applicant in accordance with § 1.248, or filed in duplicate in the event service is not possible; and (3) the petition is submitted prior to the date the application was published or the mailing of a notice of allowance under § 1.311, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate copies should be submitted only when, after diligent effort, it has not been possible to serve the applicant. Notice of a petition may be entered in lieu of bulky papers; papers not physically entered will still be publicly available when the application file wrapper is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive contents required of a public use petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be submitted in writing, must specifically identify the application to which it is directed by application number or serial number and filing date, and should include a listing of all affidavits or declarations and exhibits relied on. The petition must contain a sufficient description of the subject matter alleged to have been in 'public use' or 'on sale', including any necessary photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, or flowcharts to enable the examiner to compare the claimed subject matter to the alleged public use/on-sale subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition and accompanying papers must either (A) reflect that a copy has been served upon the applicant or applicant's attorney/agent, or (B) be filed in duplicate if service is not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte vs inter partes public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two types of public use proceedings: ex parte and inter partes. In ex parte, the petitioner is not entitled as of right to inspect the pending application. In inter partes, the pending application is a reissue application and the petitioner is privy to the contents (37 CFR 1.612).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner who was once involved in a terminated interference is treated as ex parte (no longer privy). Petitions filed on or after Feb 11, 1985 have special restrictions concerning parties to interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of restriction/nonelected claims on petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition alleges that subject matter covering both elected and nonelected claims is a statutory bar, only the part of the petition drawn to the subject matter of the elected claims will be considered initially. If a public use proceeding is instituted, it may include nonelected subject matter, and evidence adduced may be used in subsequently-filed applications without requiring a new fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner will not be heard regarding the appropriateness of any restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended identifying information for petition papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition should specifically identify the application; the following information, if known, should be placed on the petition: (A) Name of Applicant(s), (B) Application number, (C) Confirmation number, (D) Filing date, (E) Title of invention, (F) Technology Center art unit number, (G) Name of examiner assigned, (H) Current status and location of application, and the word 'ATTENTION:' followed by the area of the Office to which the petition is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition itself should be clearly identified as 'PETITION UNDER 37 CFR 1.292.' If accompanied by exhibits, those should contain identifying information to prevent separation or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions directed to a reissue application involved in litigation, the outside envelope and top right-hand portion of the petition should be marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' (preferably in a bright color).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These petitions should be hand-carried if possible to ensure prompt receipt. Copies served on applicant/attorney should be complete and the filing should include a Certificate of Service. All responses in litigation-type cases should be hand-carried to the appropriate Office area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary handling by OPLA (formal requirements review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under 37 CFR 1.292 should be forwarded to OPLA; OPLA staff will ascertain whether formal requirements of 37 CFR 1.292 have been fulfilled (timeliness, alleged use/sale >1 year before effective filing date, presence of affidavits/declarations/exhibits, duplicate or service, and fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal requirements are met and the application's status warrants consideration, OPLA forwards the petition and application file to the examiner for determination whether a prima facie case is established. Protracted paper filing is discouraged; present the best case early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness rules for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted prior to the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311. Petitions submitted after issuance of the application as a patent or abandonment will not be considered. A petition filed after the mailing of a notice of allowance will be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit petitions as soon as possible after becoming aware of the application to ensure maximum consideration. A petition submitted prior to a notice of allowance but not provided to OPLA prior to issuance may be entered but dismissed as moot. Petitions filed after final rejection may be considered if the application is still pending, but prosecution will not ordinarily be reopened if the petition's subject matter is cumulative of prior art in the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special timing and extensions for reissue petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition regarding a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following the Official Gazette announcement of the reissue. If the petition cannot be filed within this 2-month period, it may be submitted later by petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and accompanied by the petition fee in 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such extension petitions must explain why additional time is necessary and be served on applicant. Requests will be critically reviewed and granted only when necessary for the minimum additional period. 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions should be filed early; the Office may waive the 2-month delay under 37 CFR 1.183 when accompanied by the petition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification search when application not specifically identified
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner is unable to specifically identify the pending application, the petition should be directed to OPLA or 'Box DAC' with as much identifying data as possible; OPLA will forward it to the appropriate TC Director for an identification search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the application file(s) is located, it should be forwarded to OPLA for handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when service is absent or duplicate not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition does not indicate service and is not filed in duplicate, the Office will attempt to determine whether service has been made by contacting applicant or applicant's attorney/agent. If service has not been made and no duplicate has been filed, the Office may request petitioner to file a duplicate before referring to the examiner or may reproduce the petition itself to avoid delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition is not submitted prior to mailing of a notice of allowance, it should not be entered in the application file and the applicant should be notified that the petition is untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: File handling of untimely petition (service included vs not included)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition is not submitted prior to mailing of a notice of allowance, handling varies: (A) If the petition includes indication of service on applicant, the original petition should be discarded; (B) If service of copy not included, the duplicate copy (if present) should be discarded and the original petition should be sent to the applicant along with notification of nonentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures ensure applicant receives notice when petitions are untimely and not entered into the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA referral and examiner determination: prima facie showing standard
rubrics_metrics.description: After OPLA's formal review, the examiner determines whether the petition establishes a prima facie showing that the invention was in public use or on sale more than one year before the filing date so as to create a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case is established if the facts asserted in affidavits/declarations, as supported by exhibits, would, if later proved true by testimony, result in the statutory bar. The examiner must: (1) identify exactly what was in public use or on sale; (2) determine whether it was in use or on sale in this country more than one year before the effective filing date; and (3) determine whether the pending claims 'read' on or are obvious over the alleged public use/on-sale matter. The examiner should compare all pending claims with the matter alleged to have been in use or on sale, not just claims identified by petitioner.
